title: Hello AI World
summary: The whole map in one board: programming and math, machine learning, deep learning, then large language models, ML systems or computer vision — and interview prep at the end. Pick the branch that matches the job you want.

stages.title: Programming
stages.passCriteria: You can write, test and debug a Python program on your own.

stages.title: Python for Data
stages.passCriteria: You can work with NumPy arrays, and load, clean, explore and plot a dataset with pandas in a notebook.

stages.title: Calculus
stages.passCriteria: You can take derivatives and partial derivatives, compute a gradient, and apply the chain rule.

stages.title: Linear Algebra
stages.passCriteria: You can multiply matrices and explain, geometrically, what a matrix does to a vector.

stages.title: Probability & Statistics
stages.passCriteria: You can work with probability, random variables and distributions, and test a hypothesis.

stages.title: Core Machine Learning
stages.passCriteria: You can train, evaluate and compare regression and classification models.

stages.title: Neural Networks
stages.passCriteria: You can implement backpropagation from scratch and build a small GPT.

stages.title: Practice
stages.passCriteria: You can train an image or text model in PyTorch and explain each step.

stages.title: Theory
stages.passCriteria: You can explain why deep networks train: optimization, initialization, regularization and normalization.

stages.title: Attention
stages.passCriteria: You can explain how attention works and why Transformers replaced recurrent networks.

stages.title: Generative Models
stages.passCriteria: You can explain how a diffusion model turns noise into an image, and implement one.

stages.title: Transformers & NLP
stages.passCriteria: You can explain attention and implement a Transformer-based NLP model.

stages.title: LLM Training
stages.passCriteria: You can explain pretraining, fine-tuning and LoRA, and fine-tune a small model.

stages.title: RAG & Evaluation
stages.passCriteria: You can build a retrieval-augmented app end to end, compare at least two retrieval approaches, and write up where its answers fail.

stages.title: Agents
stages.passCriteria: You can build an agent that uses tools, and evaluate it.

stages.title: MLOps
stages.passCriteria: You can deploy a model, track experiments and monitor it in production.

stages.title: ML System Design
stages.passCriteria: You can design an ML system end to end and explain its trade-offs.

stages.title: Training at Scale
stages.passCriteria: You can explain mixed precision, data and model parallelism, and quantization, and when each one helps.

stages.title: Portfolio Project
stages.passCriteria: You can take one model from raw data to a deployed, tested service, show where it fails, and explain your trade-offs.

stages.title: Classical CV
stages.passCriteria: You can explain image formation, filtering, edges, features, camera calibration and stereo.

stages.title: CNNs
stages.passCriteria: You can explain how a CNN sees an image and why residual connections help.

stages.title: Vision Transformers
stages.passCriteria: You can explain how ViT and CLIP apply attention to images.

stages.title: Portfolio Project
stages.passCriteria: You can fine-tune a detector on your own dataset, evaluate it per class with mAP, show where it fails, and deploy it behind an API.

stages.title: Coding
stages.passCriteria: You can solve timed coding problems on data structures and algorithms.

stages.title: ML & DL Questions
stages.passCriteria: You can answer machine learning and deep learning knowledge and system design questions under time pressure.
